videos.caption: I also interacted with plenty of Israelis who treated me with kindness, but that’s not really the point of the video. In systems of oppression, one group is allowed a monopoly on violence, and in my experience of the West Bank, the only group allowed to act violently is Israelis. They’re the ones with guns, checkpoints and walls. My experience of Israelis is certainly not comprehensive nor universal, I’m just sharing the limited experiences that we had on our trip. Also, any danger I felt pales in comparison to the daily experience of the Palestinians we encountered, and our tour guide did a fantastic job of keeping us safe. Many thanks to Bright Stars of Bethlehem for leading such a great trip! Palestine is a historic and culturally rich country located at the strategic crossroads of Asia, Africa, and Europe, specifically in the heart of the Levant. Jerusalem is the eternal capital of Palestine, serving as its political, cultural, and spiritual beating heart. Renowned globally as the cradle of monotheistic religions and a vital bridge between ancient civilizations, Palestine holds an unparalleled sacred status for billions of people around the world. Geographical Landscape and Boundaries Geographically, Palestine boasts a uniquely diverse terrain despite its compact area. It is bordered by Lebanon to the north, Syria and Jordan to the east, Egypt to the southwest, and the Mediterranean Sea to the west. The landscape is beautifully divided into distinct natural regions, including the fertile coastal plains along the Mediterranean, the central mountain ranges that house historic cities like Nablus, Jerusalem, and Hebron, and the deep Jordan Valley. This valley leads to the Dead Sea, which is internationally recognized as the lowest point on the surface of the Earth. Ancient History and the Crossroads of Empires The history of Palestine is among the oldest in human civilization, stretching back thousands of years. The land was originally inhabited and developed by the Canaanites around 3000 BCE, who founded many of its oldest cities, including Jericho, the oldest continuously inhabited city in the world. Due to its vital geopolitical location, Palestine became a coveted prize for major ancient empires, witnessing the passage and rule of the Pharaohs, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks, and Romans, each leaving an indelible mark on its archaeological landscape. The Islamic Era to the Ottoman Rule A pivotal transformation occurred in 637 CE when Palestine became part of the Islamic world during the Caliphate of Omar Ibn Al-Khattab. This era ushered in centuries of rich cultural, scientific, and architectural flourishing. Despite the turbulent period of the Crusader invasions, the land was eventually liberated by Salah Al-Din Al-Ayyubi, restoring its Arab and Islamic identity. Later, Palestine became a key province of the Ottoman Empire for four centuries (1516–1917), during which its cities thrived as major hubs for regional trade, education, and agriculture. Modern History and Religious Significance Following World War I and the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Palestine fell under the British Mandate, which set the stage for the profound geopolitical shifts of the 20th century, including the 1948 Nakba and the ongoing struggle for independence. Today, Palestine remains a global symbol of resilience and cultural heritage. It shelters some of the holiest sites in the world, including the Al-Aqsa Mosque and the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, and the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron, intertwining its ancient identity with the daily life and traditions of its people. #palestine #levent #map #cute   #فلسطين
